Does post-decision evidence still support Permit CPU and memory resource requests/limits to change in place, without requiring a Pod or container restart.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Allow actors (e.g., users, VPA, StatefulSet, JobController) to decide how to proceed when an in-place resource resize is not possible.?

Does post-decision evidence still support Change the UpdateContainerResources CRI API to take a platform-agnostic ContainerResources parameter so that it works for Windows containers and other non-Linux runtimes, not only Linux.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Extend the ContainerStatus CRI API so the kubelet can query the CPU and memory configuration currently applied to a container.?

Does post-decision evidence still support Define, as a high-level guide rather than a detailed implementation specification, the expected behavior of a container runtime when handling resource updates.?

Does post-decision evidence still support Distinguish the desired resources declared in the Pod spec from the resources allocated to the Pod on the node and from the actual resources applied to its containers.?

Does post-decision evidence still support Expose, for each resized container resource, why the desired and actual resources differ: whether a proposed resize has not yet been accepted or rejected by the kubelet, has been accepted and is being actuated, is deferred, or has been rejected as infeasible; supplemented by Pod Events at key steps.?

Does post-decision evidence still support Motivating premise stated in the 2023 KEP text: because PodSpec container resources are immutable, changing a Pod's resource allocation requires recreating the Pod.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Avoid service disruption for stateful, batch, and low-replica workloads; availability and cost are stated concerns.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Explicit non-goal: controlling the full lifecycle of a Pod whose in-place resize failed; this is left to the actors that initiated the resize.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Changing a Pod's QoS class without a restart is a non-goal.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Changing Init Container resources without a restart is a non-goal.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Evicting lower-priority Pods to make room for a resize is a non-goal (noted as a possible future enhancement).?
Does post-decision evidence still support In-place resize is restricted to CPU and memory; updating extended resources or any other resource type is a non-goal.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Supporting CPU/memory manager policies other than the default 'None' policy is a non-goal.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Represent desired resources through mutable PodSpec fields and report allocated/applied resources through PodStatus.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Offer per-resource restart-policy choices to control how container resizes are attempted.?
Does post-decision evidence still support Model resize operation progress through states such as proposed, in progress, deferred and infeasible.?
